claim: HAP2 is a class II gamete fusogen in many eukaryotic kingdoms.
source: HAP2 is a class II gamete fusogen in many eukaryotic kingdoms.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: A crystal structure of Chlamydomonas HAP2 shows a trimeric fusion state.
source: A crystal structure of Chlamydomonas HAP2 shows a trimeric fusion state.
evidence: The manuscript presents crystallographic data and structural analysis showing HAP2 in a trimeric state.

claim: Domains D1, D2.1 and D2.2 line the 3-fold axis in the HAP2 trimer structure.
source: Domains D1, D2.1 and D2.2 line the 3-fold axis; D3 and a stem pack against the outer surface.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figure 1.

claim: D3 and a stem pack against the outer surface of the HAP2 trimer.
source: Domains D1, D2.1 and D2.2 line the 3-fold axis; D3 and a stem pack against the outer surface.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange shows that surfaces of D1, D2.2 and D3 closest to the 3-fold axis are more dynamic than exposed surfaces.
source: Surprisingly, hydrogen-deuterium exchange shows that surfaces of D1, D2.2 and D3 closest to the 3-fold axis are more dynamic than exposed surfaces.
evidence: HDX experiments were performed and the results are presented in Figure 2 and discussed in the results section.

claim: Three fusion helices in the fusion loops of each monomer expose hydrophobic residues at the trimer apex.
source: Three fusion helices in the fusion loops of each monomer expose hydrophobic residues at the trimer apex that are splayed from the 3-fold axis, leaving a solvent-filled cavity between the fusion loops in each monomer.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figures 1 and 4.

claim: The hydrophobic residues at the trimer apex are splayed from the 3-fold axis, leaving a solvent-filled cavity between the fusion loops in each monomer.
source: Three fusion helices in the fusion loops of each monomer expose hydrophobic residues at the trimer apex that are splayed from the 3-fold axis, leaving a solvent-filled cavity between the fusion loops in each monomer.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figures 1 and 4.

claim: At the base of the two fusion loops, Arg185 docks in a carbonyl cage.
source: At the base of the two fusion loops, Arg185 docks in a carbonyl cage.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figures 2C and 4C,G.

claim: Mutation of axis-proximal fusion helices has a greater effect on Chlamydomonas gamete fusion than mutation of axis-distal fusion helices.
source: Comparisons to other structures, dynamics, and the greater effect on Chlamydomonas gamete fusion of mutation of axis-proximal than axis-distal fusion helices suggest that the apical portion of each monomer could tilt toward the 3-fold axis with merger of the fusion helices into a common fusion surface.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by mutagenesis data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The apical portion of each monomer could tilt toward the 3-fold axis with merger of the fusion helices into a common fusion surface.
source: Comparisons to other structures, dynamics, and the greater effect on Chlamydomonas gamete fusion of mutation of axis-proximal than axis-distal fusion helices suggest that the apical portion of each monomer could tilt toward the 3-fold axis with merger of the fusion helices into a common fusion surface.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on structural comparisons, HDX data, and mutagenesis results.

claim: HAP2/GCS1 is essential for gamete fusion in organisms across eukaryotic kingdoms.
source: The single-pass transmembrane protein HAP2/GCS1 is essential for gamete fusion in organisms across eukaryotic kingdoms, and was likely the ancient sexual fusogen used by primitive eukaryotes before the eukaryotic radiation (Wong and Johnson, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wong and Johnson, 2010.

claim: HAP2 was likely the ancient sexual fusogen used by primitive eukaryotes before the eukaryotic radiation.
source: The single-pass transmembrane protein HAP2/GCS1 is essential for gamete fusion in organisms across eukaryotic kingdoms, and was likely the ancient sexual fusogen used by primitive eukaryotes before the eukaryotic radiation (Wong and Johnson, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wong and Johnson, 2010.

claim: HAP2 is important as a target of vaccines that block the obligate sexual life cycles of parasites including Plasmodium.
source: HAP2 is also important as a target of vaccines that block the obligate sexual life cycles of parasites including Plasmodium, and hence block transmission of malaria (Angrisano et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Angrisano et al., 2017.

claim: HAP2 from Chlamydomonas, Arabidopsis, and Tetrahymena is a class II fusion glycoprotein.
source: Recent work on HAP2 from the green alga Chlamydomonas, the flowering plant Arabidopsis, and the ciliate Tetrahymena shows that HAP2 is, in common with fusogens used by certain enveloped viruses to enter host cells, a class II fusion glycoprotein (Fédry et al., 2017; Pinello et al., 2017; Valansi et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fédry et al., 2017; Pinello et al., 2017; Valansi et al., 2017.

claim: Class II fusogens are characterized by their mainly β-sheet-containing-domains I, II, and III.
source: Class II fusogens are characterized by their mainly β-sheet-containing-domains I, II, and III (referred to here as D1, D2, and D3) (Harrison, 2015; Kielian and Rey, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Harrison, 2015; Kielian and Rey, 2006.

claim: A stem region connects the globular domains to transmembrane domains in class II fusogens.
source: A stem region connects these globular domains to two transmembrane domains in flaviviruses (Zhang et al., 2013) or a single-pass transmembrane domain and a cytoplasmic domain in eukaryotes.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2013 for flaviviruses.

claim: Sequence homology is not detectable among class II fusogens from different virus families or with HAP2.
source: Although sequence homology is not detectable among class II fusogens from different virus families or with HAP2, similar three-dimensional structures and functions suggest that they diverged from a common ancestor (Fédry et al., 2017; Pinello et al., 2017; Valansi et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fédry et al., 2017; Pinello et al., 2017; Valansi et al., 2017.

claim: Similar three-dimensional structures and functions suggest that class II fusogens diverged from a common ancestor.
source: Although sequence homology is not detectable among class II fusogens from different virus families or with HAP2, similar three-dimensional structures and functions suggest that they diverged from a common ancestor (Fédry et al., 2017; Pinello et al., 2017; Valansi et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fédry et al., 2017; Pinello et al., 2017; Valansi et al., 2017.

claim: HAP2 functions uni-directionally in Chlamydomonas.
source: As with viral class II proteins, HAP2 functions uni-directionally. Thus, in Chlamydomonas, HAP2 is expressed and required for fusion only in minus mating type gametes, and not in plus mating type gametes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is consistent with known biology of Chlamydomonas mating.

claim: In Chlamydomonas, HAP2 is expressed and required for fusion only in minus mating type gametes, and not in plus mating type gametes.
source: Thus, in Chlamydomonas, HAP2 is expressed and required for fusion only in minus mating type gametes, and not in plus mating type gametes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is consistent with known biology of Chlamydomonas mating.

claim: Chlamydomonas HAP2 glycoprotein (ectodomain residues 23 – 582) was crystallized and the structure was refined to 2.6 Å with Rwork and Rfree of 23.2% and 28.1%, respectively.
source: Chlamydomonas HAP2 glycoprotein (ectodomain residues 23 – 582) with a C-terminal His tag was secreted from Drosophila S2 cells, purified by Ni-affinity chromatography and gel filtration, and crystallized. The structure was refined to 2.6 Å with Rwork and Rfree of 23.2% and 28.1%, respectively (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by crystallographic data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Three monomers in the asymmetric unit form a trimer and pack against one another through D1 and D2 at the 3-fold axis.
source: Three monomers in the asymmetric unit form a trimer and pack against one another through D1 and D2 at the 3-fold axis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A showing the trimeric structure.

claim: D3 packs against the outer faces of D1 and D2 in the HAP2 trimer.
source: In further similarity to other class II fusion-state structures, a U-turn between D1 and D3 enables D3 to pack against the outer faces of D1 and D2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: D2 narrows at a waist that divides two subdomains termed D2.1 and D2.2.
source: D2 narrows at a waist that divides two subdomains we term D2.1 and D2.2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: D2.2 at the apical end of trimers bears three fusion helices, α1, η1, and α2, in fusion loops 1 and 2 between β-strands c and d.
source: D2.2 at the 'apical', narrower end of trimers bears three fusion helices, α1, η1, and α2, in fusion loops 1 and 2 between β-strands c and d.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A and Figure 4.

claim: Following D3, a stem segment binds in a groove in D2 of a neighboring monomer.
source: Following D3, a stem segment binds in a groove in D2 of a neighboring monomer.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: The 2.6 Å structure shows 50 more residues per monomer than the 3.3 Å structure.
source: Either as a consequence of omission of protease treatment here, differences in the crystal lattice, or higher resolution, we can visualize 50 more residues per monomer.
evidence: This is stated in the results section comparing the current structure to the previous structure.

claim: The fusion loops can be completely traced in the 2.6 Å structure, forming three helices with apically-pointing hydrophobic residues in each monomer.
source: Importantly, we can completely trace the fusion loops, which form three helices with apically-pointing hydrophobic residues in each monomer (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Of nine total fusion helices in the trimer, only one was resolved in the previous structure.
source: Of nine total fusion helices, only one was resolved in the previous structure, and it differed in orientation (Figure 1B), accounting for the markedly different appearance of the two structures in the apical portion of D2.2 (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section comparing the current structure to the previous structure shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Purified, monomeric HAP2 fortuitously trimerized into a fusion state during crystallization.
source: Purified, monomeric HAP2 fortuitously trimerized into a fusion state during crystallization.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the HDX experiments.

claim: Incubation of monomeric HAP2 with dodecylmaltoside detergent induces trimerization.
source: To obtain a trimeric, fusion-state form for HDX, we incubated monomeric HAP2 with dodecylmaltoside detergent to bind to its fusion loops and simulate membrane engagement.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Multi-angle light scattering showed that monomeric HAP2 contains 6% glycan.
source: Multi-angle light scattering showed that monomeric HAP2 contains 6% glycan, and that the glycoprotein mass of the main peak after detergent treatment was 2.99-fold greater than the monomer, in excellent agreement with trimer formation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The glycoprotein mass of the main peak after detergent treatment was 2.99-fold greater than the monomer.
source: Multi-angle light scattering showed that monomeric HAP2 contains 6% glycan, and that the glycoprotein mass of the main peak after detergent treatment was 2.99-fold greater than the monomer, in excellent agreement with trimer formation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The most dynamic regions of D1, D2.2, and D3 lie more on their faces directed toward, rather than away from, the 3-fold axis.
source: As discussed later in results, the most dynamic regions of D1, D2.2, and D3 surprisingly lie more on their faces directed toward, rather than away from, the 3-fold axis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The apical portion of D2.2 containing its fusion loops was among the most rapidly exchanging regions in HAP2.
source: The apical portion of D2.2 containing its fusion loops was among the most rapidly exchanging regions in HAP2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The small β-sheets in D2.1 and D2.2 exchanged more slowly than the larger β-sheets in D1 and D3.
source: The small β-sheets in D2.1 and D2.2 surprisingly exchanged more slowly than the larger β-sheets in D1 and D3.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Comparison between monomer and trimer HDX revealed no overall effect of trimerization; instead, differences were limited to specific regions.
source: Comparison between monomer and trimer HDX revealed no overall effect of trimerization; instead, differences were limited to specific regions (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: D1 forms the base of the HAP2 trimer.
source: D1 forms the base of the HAP2 trimer.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: The first two β-strands of D1, A0 and B0, form a long disulfide-bonded β-ribbon that extends to the β-sheet on the other face of D1 in a neighboring monomer.
source: Its first two β-strands, A0 and B0, form a long disulfide-bonded β-ribbon that is unusual in extending to the β-sheet on the other face of D1 in a neighboring monomer (Fédry et al., 2017) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section, supported by a citation to Fédry et al., 2017, and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: HDX is lower in the A0-B0 region in the trimer relative to the monomer.
source: In agreement, HDX is lower in this region in the trimer relative to the monomer (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Six disulfide-bonded cysteines in the C0-D0 loop and 18 residues in the E0-F0 loop are newly built in the 2.6 Å structure.
source: Six disulfide-bonded cysteines in the C0-D0 loop and 18 residues in the E0-F0 loop are newly built in our structure (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A,B.

claim: The E0-F0 loop has a Ser, Thr, and Pro-rich sequence that is predicted to be O-glycosylated.
source: The E0-F0 loop has a Ser, Thr, and Pro-rich sequence that is predicted to be O-glycosylated and four predicted N-glycosylation sites in the disordered region (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The E0-F0 loop has four predicted N-glycosylation sites in the disordered region.
source: The E0-F0 loop has a Ser, Thr, and Pro-rich sequence that is predicted to be O-glycosylated and four predicted N-glycosylation sites in the disordered region (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Domain 3 has two β-sheets that sandwich together with a hydrophobic core.
source: Domain 3 has two β-sheets that sandwich together with a hydrophobic core.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: D3 should be classified as an FN3 domain, since its D β-strand joins the GFC β-sheet as in FN3 domains rather than the ABE β-sheet as in Ig domains.
source: D3 is termed immunoglobulin-like; however, it should be classified as an FN3 domain, since its D β-strand joins the GFC β-sheet as in FN3 domains rather than the ABE β-sheet as in Ig domains (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: D3 closely matches the elongated FN3 domains found in complement components C3, C4, and C5, which are termed macroglobulin domains.
source: Search for structurally homologous domains (Holm et al., 2008) shows that D3 closely matches the elongated FN3 domains found in complement components C3, C4, and C5, which are termed macroglobulin domains.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to Holm et al., 2008.

claim: Faster exchange in trimers in the B-C loop suggests a structural alteration in monomers.
source: Faster exchange in trimers in the B-C loop (Figure 2D) which is well exposed to solvent but is at the end of D3 facing D1 (Figure 1A) suggests a structural alteration in monomers, consistent with their hypothesized more linear D1-D3 interface.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: D2 is formed by both β-sheets and α-helices.
source: D2 is formed by both β-sheets and α-helices.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: The slowest exchanging regions in HAP2 are found in D2.1 near its junction with D2.2.
source: The slowest exchanging regions in HAP2 are found in D2.1 near its junction with D2.2, where D2.1 has a substantial hydrophobic core underlying the right-angle junction between the slow-exchanging α4-helix and aef β-sheet (Figure 1A and Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Slowly exchanging regions in D2.2 include the lower portions of β-strands b and d and a loop with a η3-helix.
source: Slowly exchanging regions found in the thin D2.2 subdomain include the lower portions of β-strands b and d and a loop with a η3-helix.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2.

claim: These elements in D2.2 form a carbonyl cage that docks Arg185.
source: Together, these elements in D2.2 form a carbonyl cage that docks Arg185, which is present in a rapidly exchanging loop (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural and HDX data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: The apex of D2.2 including the entire β-strand c, fusion loops 1 and 2, and the portions closest to the 3-fold axis are in rapid to moderate HDX, suggesting flexibility.
source: The apex of D2.2 including the entire β-strand c, fusion loops 1 and 2, and the portions closest to the 3-fold axis are in rapid to moderate HDX, suggesting flexibility (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The d and e β-strands and the α4-helix and following loop are buried in the trimeric assembly including in an interface with D3.
source: In agreement with slower exchange in trimeric than monomeric HAP2, the d and e β-strands and the α4-helix and following loop (Figure 2D) are buried in the trimeric assembly including in an interface with D3 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2D and structural data in Figure 1A.

claim: Plasmodium HAP2 contains an even longer f-g loop with four cysteines and a long loop between η5 and the l β-strand in D2.
source: Based on its sequence, Plasmodium HAP2 contains an even longer f-g loop with four cysteines and a long loop between η5 and the l β-strand in D2 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The highly conserved 'HAP2-GCS1 domain' (PFAM PF10699), residues 352–399, lies close to the 3-fold trimer axis at the junction between D2.1 and D2.2.
source: The highly conserved 'HAP2-GCS1 domain' (PFAM PF10699), residues 352–399, lies close to the 3-fold trimer axis at the junction between D2.1 and D2.2, and largely contains loops and short η and α-helices (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Highly conserved sidechains in the HAP2-GCS1 domain form hydrophobic cores that underlie the α4-helix and aef β-sheet in D2.1 and the carbonyl cage in D2.2.
source: Highly conserved sidechains in this region form hydrophobic cores that underlie the α4-helix and aef β-sheet in D2.1 and the carbonyl cage in D2.2 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The majority of HAP2-GCS1 residues in D2.2 (360 – 380) show >40% HDX at 1 min.
source: Nonetheless, the majority of HAP2-GCS1 residues in D2.2 (360 – 380) show >40% HDX at 1 min.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by HDX data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The 360 – 380 region has exposed backbone amides, suggesting it has access to conformational change.
source: Thus, this region has exposed backbone amides, suggesting it has access to conformational change.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is an inference from HDX data.

claim: Mutations of conserved residues Asp367 and Lys368 have no effect on HAP2 function.
source: Malleability of the 360 – 380 region is further suggested by lack of effect on HAP2 function of mutations of conserved residues Asp367 and Lys368 (Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2015.

claim: The fusion loops in HAP2 lie between the c and d β-strands.
source: In common with the fusion loops of most viral class II fusogens, the fusion loops in HAP2 lie between the c and d β-strands.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The fusion loops in HAP2 are unusually long at 39 residues and have three helices.
source: The fusion loops in HAP are unusually long at 39 residues and have three helices.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Each helix (α1, η1, and α2) displays a set of two to three hydrophobic residues that project apically.
source: Each helix, α1 in loop 1, and η1 and α2 in loop 2, displays a set of two to three hydrophobic residues that project apically (Figure 4D–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4D–H.

claim: Loop 1 extends from Cys167 to Arg185 and contains the α1-helix with Trp173 and Phe177 in an apical orientation.
source: Loop 1 extends from Cys167 to Arg185 and contains the α1-helix with Trp173 and Phe177 in an apical orientation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Loop 2 lies between Arg185 and the beginning of β-strand d and contains the η1-helix with Phe192 and Trp193 that orient apically, and the α2-helix with Leu197 and Leu200 that orient apically and Ile201 that orients outward.
source: Loop 2 lies between Arg185 and the beginning of β-strand d. It contains the η1-helix with Phe192 and Trp193 that orient apcally, and the α2-helix with Leu197 and Leu200 that orient apically and Ile201 that orients outward.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The three helices in each monomer have orientations similar to three sides of a box, with axes of α1 and α2 pointing toward the 3-fold axis while the η1-helix axis forms the outer side, more distal from the 3-fold axis.
source: The three helices in each monomer have orientations similar to three sides of a box (lines in Figure 4D mark helix axes of the right-most monomer), with axes of α1 and α2 pointing toward the 3-fold axis while the η1-helix axis forms the outer side, more distal from the 3-fold axis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The division between fusion loops is defined by a basally projecting loop with Arg185 at its tip.
source: The division between fusion loops is defined by a basally projecting loop with Arg185 at its tip.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The Arg185 sidechain guanido group docks through six hydrogen bonds to its carbonyl cage formed by backbone and sidechain carbonyl oxygens in the core of subdomain D2.2.
source: The Arg185 sidechain guanido group docks through six hydrogen bonds to its carbonyl cage formed by backbone and sidechain carbonyl oxygens in the core of subdomain D2.2 (Figures 2C and 4C,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figures 2C and 4C,G.

claim: The architecture of the 3-helix fusion surface in each HAP2 monomer is well supported by a hydrophobic core that underlies and knits together the α1, η1, and α2-helices and a robust network of hydrogen bonds.
source: The architecture of the 3-helix fusion surface in each HAP2 monomer is well supported by a hydrophobic core that underlies and knits together the α1, η1, and α2-helices and a robust network of hydrogen bonds (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: HAP2 ectodomain monomers utilize their fusion loops to bind phospholipid vesicles and detergent as shown by induction of trimerization.
source: HAP2 ectodomain monomers appear to utilize their fusion loops to bind phospholipid vesicles (Fédry et al., 2017) and detergent (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) as shown by induction of trimerization.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to Fédry et al., 2017 and data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the crystal structure, D2.2 splays away from the 3-fold axis so that the 3-helix fusion surfaces of monomers are separated from one another by solvent.
source: In the crystal structure, however, D2.2 splays away from the 3-fold axis so that the 3-helix fusion surfaces of monomers are separated from one another by solvent (Figure 4A and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4A and D.

claim: The crystal structure may represent an early fusion state of HAP2 that precedes a more mature state in which reorientation could allow the fusion loops in each monomer to approach and close up at the 3-fold axis to form a common fusion surface.
source: These apparent barriers raise the possibility that our crystal structure represents an early fusion state of HAP2 that precedes a more mature state in which reorientation could allow the fusion loops in each monomer to approach and close up at the 3-fold axis to form a common fusion surface.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is a speculation based on structural observations.

claim: The two HAP2 crystal structures superimpose extremely well on D1, D2.1, and D3.
source: The two HAP2 crystal structures superimpose extremely well on D1, D2.1, and D3 (Figure 5B); however, orientations at their D2.1-D2.2 junctions differ (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 5.

claim: Orientations at the D2.1-D2.2 junctions differ between the two HAP2 crystal structures.
source: The two HAP2 crystal structures superimpose extremely well on D1, D2.1, and D3 (Figure 5B); however, orientations at their D2.1-D2.2 junctions differ (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The three monomers in the current HAP2 structure have essentially identical D2.1-D2.2 orientations.
source: While the three monomers in our HAP2 structure have essentially identical D2.1-D2.2 orientations, monomers in the previous structure differ; Figure 5A–B displays one monomer from our structure and two from the previous structure.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 5A–B.

claim: HAP2 and Tick-borne encephalitis fusogens show similar flexibility at the D2.1 and D2.2 junction.
source: Interestingly, the HAP2 and Tick-borne encephalitis fusogens show similar flexibility at the D2.1 and D2.2 junction (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: The flexibility at the D2.1-D2.2 junction in HAP2 and Tick-borne encephalitis is comparable in extent (up to ~2 Å) and in exhibiting both radial and circumferential motion.
source: Their flexibility is comparable in extent (up to ~2 Å) and in exhibiting both radial and circumferential motion.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 5.

claim: Among flavivirus fusion state structures, perhaps the largest difference in orientation at the D1-D2.1 junction is seen between Dengue 1 and St. Louis encephalitis flavivirus fusogens.
source: Among flavivirus fusion state structures, perhaps the largest difference in orientation at the D1-D2.1 junction is seen between Dengue 1 and St. Louis encephalitis flavivirus fusogens (Figure 5E,F and Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 5E,F and Figure 6.

claim: Viral class II fusogens flex at the D1-D2.1 junction between their pre-fusion and fusion states.
source: Viral class II fusogens also flex at the D1-D2.1 junction between their pre-fusion and fusion states (Harrison, 2015; Kielian and Rey, 2006) and to a lesser extent at the D2.1-D2.2 junction.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to Harrison, 2015; Kielian and Rey, 2006.

claim: Flexibility visualized in comparison between flavivirus fusion state structures has both radial and circumferential components.
source: Flexibility visualized in comparison between flavivirus fusion state structures has both radial and circumferential components (Figure 5E–F) and is larger in extent than seen in the examples of D2.1-D2.2 flexion with HAP2 and Tick-borne encephalitis (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 5.

claim: Of the fusion loop segment from residue 167 to 204, only fragments from residue 182 to 194 (monomer A) or from residue 184 to 190 or 191 (monomers B and C) were built in the previous structure.
source: Of the fusion loop segment from residue 167 to 204, only fragments from residue 182 to 194 (monomer A) or from residue 184 to 190 or 191 (monomers B and C) were built in the previous structure.
evidence: This is stated in the results section comparing the current structure to the previous structure.

claim: The entirety of the fusion loop segments built in the previous structure differs from that in the current structure.

We thus tested whether fusion of a Chlamydomonas hap2 mutant could be rescued by transformation with hemagglutinin (HA)-tagged HAP2 (HAP2-HA) transgenes bearing mutations in the α1-helix (W173A/F177A, fh1), η1-helix (F192A/W193A, fh2), or α2-helix (L197A/L200A/I201A, fh3).

source: Immunoblotting showed the typical HAP2 doublet with a larger surface-expressed form and a smaller, intracellular form (Liu et al., 2015) in hap2 gametes expressing wild-type and all three mutants forms of HAP2-HA (wt-, fh1-, fh2-, and fh3), and as expected, not in wild-type plus gametes (wt+) (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Trypsin-treated gametes lost the upper but not lower HAP2 band, indicating surface localization.
source: Furthermore, trypsin-treated gametes lost the upper but not lower HAP2 band (Figure 7B).

claim: Wild-type and each mutant HAP2 were present between the two cilia at the site of the minus mating structure.

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The three fusion helix mutations gave rise to HAP2 proteins that were of the correct size in SDS-PAGE, surface-expressed as shown by trypsin susceptibility, and localized to the mating structure as shown by microscopy.
source: Thus, the three fusion helix mutations gave rise to HAP2 proteins that were of the correct size in SDS-PAGE, surface-expressed as shown by trypsin susceptibility, and localized to the mating structure as shown by microscopy.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is a summary of the data shown in Figure 7A-C.

claim: fh minus gametes were as capable of ciliary adhesion as wild-type minus gametes when mixed with plus gametes.
source: Cellular agglutination as measured by electronic particle counting showed that fh minus gametes were indeed as capable of ciliary adhesion as wild-type minus gametes when mixed with plus gametes (Figure 7E).

claim: Cell wall loss was robust and indistinguishable from wild-type in fh mutants.
source: Cell wall loss, as measured by the susceptibility of wall-less but not walled gametes to mild detergent-mediated release into the supernatant of cytoplasmic contents including OD435-detectable chlorophyll, was robust and indistinguishable from wild-type in fh mutants (Figure 7F), showing that they became activated.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: All three fh mutants were competent in mating structure adhesion.

claim: Fusion with wild-type HAP2-HA gametes was nearly 50% after 5 min and over 80% by 30 min.

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7I.

claim: Fusion was essentially absent in the fh1 and fh3 mutants (maximal fusion was <1% in fh1 and <2% in fh3).

claim: W173 and F177 in the α1-helix and L197, L200, and I201 in the α2-helix were essential for fusion.
source: These results demonstrate that the apically exposed, hydrophobic residues in each of the helices in the HAP2 fusion loops are indeed important in cell fusion during Chlamydomonas fertilization. Furthermore, W173 and F177 in the α1-helix mutated in fh1 and L197, L200, and I201 in the α2-helix mutated in fh3 were essential for fusion, while F192 and W193 in the more distal η1-helix mutated in fh2 were only moderately, albeit significantly, required for fusion.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is a conclusion from the mutagenesis data shown in Figure 7I.

claim: F192 and W193 in the η1-helix were only moderately, albeit significantly, required for fusion.
source: These results demonstrate that the apically exposed, hydrophobic residues in each of the helices in the HAP2 fusion loops are indeed important in cell fusion during Chlamydomonas fertilization. Furthermore, W173 and F177 in the α1-helix mutated in fh1 and L197, L200, and I201 in the α2-helix mutated in fh3 were essential for fusion, while F192 and W193 in the more distal η1-helix mutated in fh2 were only moderately, albeit significantly, required for fusion.

In this model, the HAP2 crystal structure represents an intermediate state in fusion.

source: Pivoting or iris-like movements in D2.1 and/or D2.2 during the fusion reaction result in a unitary fusion surface with essential, axis-proximal α1- and α2-helices at the center of a membrane interaction surface, and less-necessary, axis-distal η1 helices at the periphery.

claim: The fusion surfaces of each monomer move towards the 3-fold axis to form a single, large fusion surface in the final state for membrane fusion.
source: Correspondingly, we propose that the transition state is the most sensitive state to mutation, and therefore that the fusion surfaces of each monomer move towards the 3-fold axis to form a single, large fusion surface in the final state for membrane fusion, which would also likely be the state in which the fusion loops are most deeply buried in the membrane.

claim: Tilting at the D1—D2.1 junction resulting in iris-like motion of fusion loops, tilting at the D2.1—D2.2 junction, and rocking of fusion loops in the carbonyl cage may all contribute to the approach toward the 3-fold axis of the fusion loops in HAP2.

source: The orientation with respect to the 3-fold axis of the three, hydrophobic residue-bearing helices within each monomer of HAP2 are likely to change little during movement toward the 3-fold axis, as seen in flavivirus fusogens.
